alt: Stop copying the same order into three places.
One order, three copies: The order arrives - In a chat, form or store.; Stock gets updated - By hand, in a sheet.; The team is told - Another message to write.
Every copy is a chance to slip. A typo, a missed update, a late message. And the same typing repeats every day, for every order.
Hypothetical example. Example: one order, one flow: The order is entered once - In one place only.; Stock updates from it - No second entry.; The team gets one alert - With the order details.
Copying vs connected. Copy and paste: Three entries per order; Easy to miss one. One flow: One entry per order; Updates follow on their own
Add checkpoints: Item out of stock - A person decides.; Unclear address - A person confirms.; Unusual large order - A person reviews.
Before you automate: Where does an order arrive?; Where is it copied?; Who needs to know?; Which cases need a person?

caption:
Stop copying the same order into three places. 🔁

When an order has to be typed into a chat, a stock sheet and a team message, each copy takes time and each one can go wrong.

A better flow starts with a map: where does the order arrive, where is it copied, who needs to know, and which cases need a person to decide. Automate the routine steps, and keep checkpoints for out-of-stock items, unclear addresses and unusual orders.

The example in the carousel is hypothetical.
